properties.statement:
A SESSION'S GRAPH WRITES WENT UNEXPORTED BECAUSE THE SERVED INSTRUCTIONS IMPLY THE SHARED SERVER MUST BE STOPPED FIRST. IT MUST NOT. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, item 12 — recorded as a DOCUMENTATION defect, because the report's own reasoning is what turned out to be wrong.

HIS CLAIM: 'This session wrote more and did not refresh the export (shared server holds the store; EXPORT WANTS IT STOPPED). Agents will not `--stop-shared` in the middle of a user-facing debug loop.' The behavioural prediction is sound. The premise is false.

MEASURED HERE, 2026-08-15: `export_graph` takes a READ LOCK on the in-process graph (`crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/exchange.rs:128`) and never opens the store directly. It is callable at any time, from any session, with a shared server running — this session called it repeatedly while the daemon held the store. ONLY the CLI `--import` / `--export` path, which opens RocksDB itself, needs `--stop-shared`.

WHERE THE MISTAKE COMES FROM, AND IT IS OURS: the served AGENTS.md section 'Restoring a design' says a command which opens the store DIRECTLY cannot run while the server holds it, gives the `--stop-shared` + `--import` recipe, and then says '`--export` writes one back out' — in the same breath, with no signal that the MCP TOOL of nearly the same name is unaffected. A careful reader generalises the caveat to both, which is what happened.

COST: a full session of design work — ChangeEvents, snapshots, Decision and Requirement merges, Artifact checksums — left unexported and therefore invisible to every other seat, because of one paragraph's arrangement. And the session was RIGHT that it would not stop a shared server mid-debug; it simply never needed to.

FIX SHAPE: separate the CLI paragraph from the tool, and say plainly that `export_graph` needs no stop. `fact:defect-the-served-instructions-put-their-standing-rules-where-a-client-cap-deletes-them` is the sibling finding about the same document's shape.
